appendix64.heading_as_printed: Appendix 64. IV ix 50 (p. 233, 8) according to F².
appendix64.heading_translation: Appendix 64. IV ix 50 (p. 233, line 8), according to F².
appendix64.latin_excerpt: Ut fugientes securi vadant. Cum autem Luna hanc peragraverit mansionem, facias in ferro ymaginem hominis pedibus alati et in capite galeam habentis. Et ipsam cum argento vivo suffumigabis; et dicas: Tu, Geliel, facias talem ferrentem hoc sigillum ut securus vadat et aufugiat a quocumque loco. Et hoc sigillum quicumque portaverit securus fugiet. Et scias quod Geliel est nomen domini istius mansionis.
appendix64.translation: So that fugitives may go safely. When the Moon has traversed this mansion, make in iron an image of a man with winged feet and a helmet on his head. Fumigate it with quicksilver and say: You, Geliel, make such a bearer of this seal that he may go safely and flee from whatever place. Whoever carries this seal will flee safely. Know that Geliel is the name of the lord of this mansion.
appendix64.translation_caution: The phrase facias talem ferrentem is syntactically awkward; the translation preserves its apparent image/seal instruction without silently emending it.
appendix64.witness_content: The printed superscript ² is part of the F² citation and is repeated in the footnotes. The consulted sigla list defines F but does not explain the superscript as a separate manuscript; this audit therefore does not expand F² into an unverified hand or codex.

appendix65.heading_as_printed: Appendix 65. IV ix 50 according to M in marg. and to N.
appendix65.heading_translation: Appendix 65. IV ix 50 according to M in the margin and N.
appendix65.latin_excerpt: 22 mansio est Sadahaca, et est ad ligandum linguas hominum ne male dicant de te. Et quando Luna est in hac mansione, faciant annulum ferreum, in quo sculpent figuram hominis alatis pedibus, in capite galeam ferentis. Et suffumigant cum argento vivo; et sigillabant cum hac ymagine ex ferro pro securitate fugientium. Et dicas: Tu, Geliel, liga linguam talis ne de me maledicat et fac ut secure evadat ab inimicis suis. Et portat secum hunc annulum quando fugiet, et sigillat in cera nigra cum annulo quando ligat linguas.
appendix65.translation: The twenty-second mansion is Sadahaca, and it is for binding people's tongues so that they do not speak ill of you. When the Moon is in this mansion, make an iron ring in which you carve the figure of a man with winged feet and wearing a helmet on his head. Fumigate it with quicksilver, and seal with this iron image for the safety of fugitives. Say: You, Geliel, bind the tongue of such a one lest he curse me, and make him escape safely from his enemies. He carries the ring with him when he flees, and seals it in black wax with the ring when he binds tongues.
apparatus_notes: fugientum is M²; fug iendum is N (printed correction: fugientum M², fugiendum N)

F.intro_location: Introduction, The Manuscripts, printed p. XIX
F.verified_provenance: Florence, Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale, Magliabechi XX 20; 117 ff.; copying finished at Brisighella near Faenza on 21 May 1536; from the Marmi collection.
F.date: early sixteenth century witness, with copying finished 21 May 1536

M.siglum_entry: M. London, BL, Sloane 3679. Class IV.
M.intro_location: Introduction, The Manuscripts, printed p. XIX
M.verified_provenance: London, British Library, Sloane 3679; 158 pp.; copied in the early seventeenth century. The introduction says it was probably copied from the manuscript acquired by Richard Napier from Simon Forman in 1599 or shortly thereafter.

N.siglum_entry: N. London, BL, Sloane 1305. Class IV.
N.intro_location: Introduction, The Manuscripts, printed p. XX
N.verified_provenance: The prose manuscript description says London, British Library, Sloane 1302, 153 ff.; probably the quarto Ashmole gave Lilly in exchange for M. It says N was probably copied in November and December 1647 and used M as its model.
N.catalogue_number_correction: The prose description gives Sloane 1302, while the printed SIGLA entry gives Sloane 1305. Both readings are present in the cached edition; this audit preserves the discrepancy and does not choose between them.

sigla_and_provenance.class_relation: F is listed in Class III. M and N are listed in Class IV; the introduction explicitly calls N a copy of M. Thus F² and M/N are separate classified witness branches, while M marginal material and N belong to one Class-IV witness series.

decision.same_series: Only in the broad bibliographic sense: both appendices are Pingree's Picatrix appendices for the same IV ix 50 passage. They are not the same witness citation. Appendix 64 is F² (Class III); Appendix 65 combines M marginal material and N (Class IV, with N described as copied from M).
decision.relation_to_all_good: Neither appendix supplies the purpose 'to acquire all good'. Appendix 64 explicitly concerns safe flight/fugitives; Appendix 65 explicitly concerns binding tongues, with safe escape as a secondary instruction. Their shared Geliel, Moon-mansion, winged-man, helmet, quicksilver, and iron-object material does not make their purposes identical.
decision.source_conclusion: Appendices 64 and 65 are distinct local witness presentations of IV ix 50 and are both distinct from the all-good purpose. They cannot be used as an exact recovered heading for the missing all-good row without another witness or textual argument.
